sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At the heart of Space Jump is its core gameplay mechanic: the jump. Simply put, the game requires you to click on the screen to jump from one planet to another. Sounds easy, right? Well, it's not as simple as it sounds. The twist is that each planet has a limited time window for jumping, and the window gets smaller as the game progresses. To make matters more difficult, the planets are randomly generated, meaning that each jump is a new challenge. The game requires you to time your jumps perfectly to avoid falling back to Earth and losing a life. With each successful jump, you earn points, and the goal is to collect as many points as possible while avoiding obstacles and making it to the next planet.

As you progress through the game, the obstacles become more challenging. Some planets have obstacles like asteroids, black holes, or even giant spaceships that can harm your character. The obstacles are randomly generated, just like the planets, so you need to stay alert and react quickly to avoid them. The game also features a variety of power-ups that can help you on your journey. These power-ups include items like shields, magnets, and boosters that can be used to overcome obstacles or gain an advantage.

To succeed in Space Jump, you need to have good timing and reaction skills. The game requires you to think quickly and make split-second decisions to avoid obstacles and make it to the next planet. With each successful jump, you earn experience points, and the goal is to level up and unlock new characters, gameplays, and power-ups. The game also features a leaderboard, where you can compare your scores with other players and try to climb the ranks.
